question.prompt: A segment through the focus \(F\) of a parabola with vertex \(V\) is perpendicular to \(\overline{FV}\) and intersects the parabola in points \(A\) and \(B.\) What is \(\cos(\angle AVB)?\)

solutions.explanation:
The focus-directrix definition determines the chord lengths relative to \(VF\), so we do not need a particular size of parabola. Let \(VF=p>0\). The directrix is perpendicular to \(VF\), on the opposite side of \(V\) from \(F\), and \(p\) units from \(V\).

The line through \(F\) perpendicular to \(VF\) is parallel to the directrix and \(2p\) units from it. Every point of the parabola is equally far from the focus and the directrix. Consequently, its two intersections with this line are \(2p\) units from \(F\), in opposite directions. Thus
\[
FA=FB=2p,\qquad AB=4p.
\]
The triangles \(VFA\) and \(VFB\) are right at \(F\), so the Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
VA=VB=\sqrt{p^2+(2p)^2}=\sqrt5\,p.
\]
Let \(\theta=\angle AVB\). In the nondegenerate triangle \(AVB\), the side opposite \(\theta\) is \(AB\). The cosine law therefore gives
\[
\cos\theta
=\frac{VA^2+VB^2-AB^2}{2VA\cdot VB}
=\frac{5p^2+5p^2-16p^2}{10p^2}
=\boxed{-\frac35}.
\]
The denominator is positive because \(p>0\). The answer is choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Find the triangle's sides from the parabola definition
Use focus-directrix distances and the cosine law
